ProgramName: Graduate Catalog
Description: The 'Graduate Catalog' is the official publication containing the academic policies, program listings, and course descriptions for The University of Memphis. As it is not a specific degree program, the following data represents the general admission requirements for the Graduate School, which may vary by specific program.

ProgramName: Online Programs
Description: The University of Memphis, through UofM Global, offers a wide array of fully online graduate degree and certificate programs across numerous disciplines. These programs are designed to provide flexibility for students whose schedules or locations make on-campus attendance difficult. UofM Global offers programs in areas such as business, education, health, engineering, and the arts and sciences.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Grants, Loans, Work-study programs

ProgramName: Graduate Programs
Description: The University of Memphis offers over 120 graduate degree programs, enrolling approximately 4,900 graduate students.  As a major urban research university holding an R1 designation, its programs are designed for both full-time students and working professionals, with many available fully online.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) in Accounting program provides a balanced, integrative approach to business education, serving the needs of students, the accounting profession, and the business community.  The curriculum is designed to help students develop critical thinking skills for making decisions on accounting and other business problems.  It requires completion of the Fogelman College's BBA requirements in addition to the specific courses for the accounting major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Advertising
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Advertising program provides students with extensive training in the written, visual, oral, and critical thinking skills necessary for a career in advertising and marketing communications. The curriculum prepares students for various strategic communication roles in agencies, private industry, and the public sector. Students gain practical experience in research, media planning, creative design, and digital marketing, often culminating in a professional portfolio.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African and African American Studies
Concentration: African-American Political Thought and Philosophy, Arts, Literature and Cultural Expression, Histories, Cultures and Institutions
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in African and African American Studies provides an in-depth look at the varied experiences and rich histories of African peoples and their descendants.  This interdisciplinary program gives students the skills to analyze the historical, cultural, and societal impacts of African migrations.  The curriculum draws from fields like history, anthropology, sociology, and political science to provide a well-rounded understanding of the subject.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Sign Language and Deaf Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in American Sign Language (ASL) and Deaf Studies is a foundational degree that immerses students in ASL, introduces them to Deaf culture and the fundamentals of communication and hearing, and prepares them to be advocates for both ASL and Deaf culture.  This degree is grounded in a broad liberal arts tradition and emphasizes a developmental sequence of language courses, along with courses in Deaf Culture, ASL linguistics, and advocacy.  Graduates will have functional skills in ASL, an understanding of Deaf history and culture, and a fundamental knowledge of communication science.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology at the University of Memphis explores human culture, evolution, behavior, beliefs, and social structures from local and global perspectives. The program develops skills in cross-cultural communication, critical thinking, analysis, and problem-solving, preparing students for careers that require an understanding of multicultural dynamics. Students have the opportunity for training in three of the four subfields: cultural and biological anthropology and archaeology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Architecture
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts with a major in Architecture is a pre-professional degree.  At the University of Memphis, the professional degree in Architecture is the Master of Architecture degree which is accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB).  All applicants must submit an application, a writing assignment, and a portfolio for an Entrance Evaluation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art - Art Education Concentration
Description: In the Art Education concentration at the University of Memphis, students focus on developing the knowledge, skills, and pedagogical approaches necessary to become effective art teachers. The program combines artistic exploration, pedagogical theory, and practical teaching experiences. Students build a strong foundation in various media like drawing, painting, and sculpture to develop their own artistic skills before delving into educational theories and instructional strategies tailored for the art classroom.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art - Fashion Design Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Art with a Fashion Design Concentration is a 120-credit hour program. It provides a comprehensive education covering university general education, major core art subjects, and specialized courses in fashion design, including sketching, textiles, sewing, and construction.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art - Fashion Merchandising Concentration
Description: In the fashion merchandising concentration at The University of Memphis, students focus on developing a comprehensive understanding of the fashion industry and acquiring the skills needed for successful merchandising and retail management. Students study fashion and consumer behavior, exploring how trends are established and how consumer preferences shape the market. The curriculum covers trend analysis, buying strategies, marketing, visual merchandising, and retail operations.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art - Global Art Histories Concentration
Description: In the Global Art Histories concentration at the University of Memphis, students focus on the history, theory, and analysis of art, delving into various artistic periods, styles, and cultural contexts to develop a deep understanding of the visual arts. The program emphasizes art historical research and methodology, where students learn to conduct research, analyze sources, write scholarly essays, and develop critical thinking skills. Visits to museums and galleries are often incorporated, and specialized courses explore themes like gender and art, postcolonial perspectives, and the intersection of art and technology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art - Graphic Design Concentration
Concentration: Graphic Design, Art Education, Photography, Studio Arts
Description: In the Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art with a Graphic Design Concentration, students focus on developing a solid foundation in the principles and techniques of graphic design. The curriculum covers the effective use of typography, imagery, and color, and students gain proficiency in industry-standard design software. The program emphasizes hands-on projects, including the design of logos, posters, and websites, and culminates in a capstone project and final exhibition.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, International grants, Tuition waivers

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art - Photography Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art with a Photography Concentration at the University of Memphis provides students with a strong artistic and conceptual foundation. Students begin with core courses in studio art and drawing before undergoing a competitive portfolio review for formal acceptance into the photography concentration. The curriculum focuses on developing technical skills, creative expression, and a deep understanding of the art world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art - Studio Arts Concentration
Concentration: Studio Arts, Painting, Sculpture, Printmaking, Ceramics
Description: In the studio arts concentration, students focus on developing their artistic skills, exploring various media, and cultivating their creative expression. Through a combination of hands-on studio work, art history courses, and critical feedback, students focus on honing their artistic skills, expanding their artistic vocabulary, and deepening their understanding of the art world. Admission to the concentration is selective and is based on a portfolio evaluation that reflects professional standards and meets concentration expectations.
ProgramCategory: Art##Studio Arts##Fine Arts##Visual and Performing Arts
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, International grants, Tuition waivers

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art - Visual Arts Concentration
Description: In the visual arts concentration, students focus on honing their artistic skills, expanding their creative expression, and developing a conceptual understanding of the visual arts.  Through a combination of studio practice, art history studies, and critical analysis, students engage in a variety of disciplines and media to cultivate their artistic voice.  In studio practice, students immerse themselves in hands-on art-making, exploring various media such as drawing, painting, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, photography, and digital art.
ProgramCategory: Art##Fine Arts##Studio Arts##Visual and Performing Arts

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Biology program aims to provide students with a thorough understanding of biological principles across all levels of organization. The curriculum is designed to develop skills in analytical reasoning, problem-solving, and laboratory techniques, preparing graduates for competitive entry into graduate and professional programs or for employment in science-related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology, Environmental Science Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Biology with an Environmental Science Concentration provides a comprehensive foundation in biological principles with a specific focus on environmental issues. The interdisciplinary nature of the concentration broadens the scope of the biology degree, while advanced biology electives allow students to tailor their education towards specific areas of interest. Students gain skills in analytical reasoning, problem-solving, and functioning in laboratory and field settings.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Business Economics
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration in Business Economics integrates economics with core business courses in marketing, management, accounting, finance, and quantitative analysis. The program provides students with the skills to gather and analyze data to solve problems for companies, governments, and non-profit organizations. It offers a strong theoretical and professional foundation for careers in both the private and public sectors.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Business Economics, Financial Economics Concentration
Description: The BBA in Economics with a concentration in Financial Economics provides a broader and deeper understanding of finance theory and practice. This program helps students develop critical thinking skills and computational tools useful in the field of finance, preparing them to make real-world financial decisions. Students learn economic theory, financial modeling, and financial management, and how to apply economic and financial analysis to problem-solving.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Business Information and Technology
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration in Business Information and Technology focuses on the essential role of information in decision-making for both managers and non-managers. The program provides knowledge in decision tools, computer and communication technology, systems design, and data management. This equips students with the skills to ensure information is understandable, timely, and relevant for appropriate individuals within an organization.
ProgramCategory: Business Administration##Business Information Systems##Information Technology##Information Systems

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry - Biochemistry Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Chemistry with a Biochemistry Concentration provides a strong foundation in chemical principles and biological systems, preparing students for postgraduate studies in health professions like pharmacy, medicine, or dentistry, as well as for careers as professional chemists. The curriculum integrates foundational chemistry with advanced biochemistry topics, emphasizing critical thinking, laboratory skills, and practical applications. This program is approved by the American Chemical Society (ACS), and graduates with the B.S.Ch. degree are certified by the ACS.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry in Chemistry - Biochemistry Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Chemistry with a Biochemistry concentration is designed for students preparing for postgraduate study in fields like pharmacy, medicine, or dentistry, or for those intending to become professional chemists.  This program is approved by the American Chemical Society Committee on Professional Training, and graduates are certified by the ACS.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry - General Concentration
Concentration: General, Biochemistry, Environmental Chemistry, Forensic Chemistry
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Chemistry with a General Concentration is recommended for students interested in teaching high school chemistry or pursuing entry-level positions in the chemical industry.  It provides the minimum coverage expected for admission to most graduate programs in chemistry.  The program requires a total of 120 credit hours to graduate, with a minimum of 42 hours at the upper-division level.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry in Chemistry - General Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science with a major in Chemistry is recommended for students interested in teaching high school chemistry or pursuing entry-level positions in the chemical industry. It provides the minimum coverage expected for admission to most graduate programs in chemistry. The degree requires 120 total hours to graduate, with at least 42 hours at the upper division.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry-Environmental Chemistry Concentration
Concentration: Environmental Chemistry, Biochemistry, Forensic Chemistry, General
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Chemistry with an Environmental Chemistry concentration is a blend of earth science and analytical chemistry, where students explore chemical phenomena in soil, atmospheric, and aquatic environments.  Students learn about the natural environment's functions and the impact of human activities on it.  The program aims to provide a strong foundation in the core concepts of chemistry, develop critical problem-solving skills, and prepare students for entry-level positions or further graduate studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry-Forensic Chemistry Concentration
Concentration: Forensic Chemistry, Biochemistry, Environmental Chemistry, General
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Chemistry with a Forensic Chemistry concentration is designed to prepare students for professional careers as chemists, particularly for those intending to work in forensic science laboratories or pursue graduate studies in the field. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in analytical, organic, physical, inorganic, and bio-organic chemistry, with specialized training in the application of chemical principles to criminal investigation. Students develop critical thinking, laboratory, and communication skills necessary for entry-level positions or advanced education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Commercial Aviation
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Commercial Aviation prepares students for careers as professional pilots for airlines, corporate aviation, government agencies, and flight schools. In addition to flight training, the curriculum includes studies in management, business operations, human resources, transportation, and aviation administration. The program combines these studies with flight labs, experiential learning, and internships to provide students with the necessary skills for employment.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, International grants, Tuition waivers

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication - Communication Studies Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Communication at the University of Memphis provides students with a comprehensive understanding of communication and media theories and methods. The program aims to develop competence in producing and analyzing messages across various media and contexts, while also emphasizing ethical principles and the role of communication in responding to societal issues. Students will gain skills in performance, critical thinking, and understanding the impact of media on communication processes.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence Concentration
Concentration: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Data Science, General
Description: The Department of Computer Science offers a Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science with an optional concentration in Artificial Intelligence. The program provides students with the skills to analyze complex computing problems and apply principles of computing to identify solutions. This degree program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (CAC/ABET).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Cybersecurity Concentration
Concentration: Cybersecurity, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, General
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science with a Cybersecurity Concentration at the University of Memphis prepares students for the growing field of cybersecurity.  The program provides a strong technical foundation in computer science and includes 12 credit hours of specialized coursework in areas like computer security, network and mobile security, and digital forensics.  The university is recognized as a National Center of Academic Excellence in Cyber Defense Education and Research (CAE-CDE, CAE-R) by the NSA/DHS.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Data Science Concentration
Concentration: Data Science, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, General
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science with a Data Science Concentration provides students with a strong foundation in programming, algorithms, and data analysis. This program focuses on the practical applications and advanced techniques in data science, preparing graduates for careers as data analysts, software engineers, and machine learning specialists. The curriculum integrates specialized coursework in data analysis, visualization, statistical methods, and machine learning.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, General Concentration
Concentration: General, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science degree at the University of Memphis prepares students to be well-rounded computer scientists with a core curriculum covering foundational math, programming, data structures, computer architecture, and software engineering. The program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET. Students can customize their degree with specialized courses and have opportunities to engage in an accelerated bachelor's/master's program and internships.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Criminology and Criminal Justice
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Criminology and Criminal Justice at the University of Memphis offers a comprehensive program exploring the multifaceted issues of crime and justice. The curriculum covers critical topics in law enforcement, corrections, policing strategies, violence prevention, and international crime. This program prepares students for diverse careers in criminal justice, law enforcement, victim advocacy, and policy analysis by equipping them with a deep understanding of the criminal justice system and critical skills to address complex societal issues.
ProgramCategory: Criminology##Criminal Justice##Law, Public Policy, and Society

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences program provides a foundation for careers in education, government, environmental professions, and research, while also preparing students for graduate studies.  The program aims to give students an understanding of Earth's fundamental principles, the environmental effects of natural and human activities, and the ability to solve geographic problems using quantitative methods.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences, Environmental Science Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences with an Environmental Science Concentration focuses on the complex interactions between the atmosphere, lithosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere. The program prepares students to address environmental challenges through understanding natural processes and human impacts. Graduates are equipped with skills in quantitative methods, geographic information science, and field methods for careers in environmental protection, conservation, and management.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences, Geoarchaeology Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences with a Geoarchaeology Concentration provides a comprehensive education in understanding Earth's processes and their relationship to archaeological landscapes.  The program integrates geology, archaeology, geography, and environmental science to analyze past human interactions with their environments.  Students gain foundational knowledge in earth materials, surface processes, and sedimentology, alongside training in archaeological methods and landscape analysis.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences, Geography Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences with a Geography concentration provides students with an understanding of the fundamental principles of Earth Sciences and the effects of natural processes and human activity on the environment. The program aims to equip students with the skills to address and solve geographic problems using quantitative methods and geographic techniques. It prepares them for job opportunities in education, government, environmental professions, and research.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences, Geology Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Earth Sciences with a Geology concentration aims to prepare students with the knowledge, skills, and experience to understand the dynamic processes of Earth's interior and surface. The program provides a foundation for careers in education, government, and environmental professions, as well as for graduate studies. The skills and knowledge acquired are particularly relevant across STEM workforces.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Economics instills habits of critical thinking and decision-making, and provides research and analytical skills that are valued in many professions.  The program explores the systems that govern the production, consumption, and exchange of goods and services, as well as how populations manage scarce resources.  This degree prepares students for careers in finance, banking, public administration, and journalism, and is also excellent preparation for Law School.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English
Concentration: African-American Literature, Applied Linguistics, Creative Writing, Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages, Literature, Professional Writing
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in English at the University of Memphis aims to develop students' skills in critical thinking, reading, and writing. The program allows students to explore the relationships between language, literature, and culture, with options to focus their studies in specific areas of interest.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English - African-American Literature Concentration
Concentration: African-American Literature, Applied Linguistics, Creative Writing, Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages, Literature, Professional Writing
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in African-American Literature is designed to familiarize students with the chronological development of African American Literature from 1750 to the present. The program aims to develop students' skills in critical thinking, reading, and writing. It prepares students for various careers, including teaching, social media management, and public relations.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English - Applied Linguistics Concentration
Concentration: African-American Literature, Creative Writing, Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages, Applied Linguistics, Literature, Professional Writing
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in English with an Applied Linguistics Concentration at the University of Memphis provides students with the necessary tools to investigate language as a system.  Students explore the theories and methods of language study and its real-world applications in fields such as literature, English as a Second Language (ESL), and composition.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Video Production, Communication
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Film and Video Production at The University of Memphis combines technical instruction with courses in motion picture studies to provide students with the skills necessary to function in the multifaceted world of film and video production.  The program's approach is broad, catering to both independent artists and those aiming to enter the film industry, ensuring each student receives personal faculty attention.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance at the University of Memphis is a rigorous program that equips students with the analytical and problem-solving skills needed for various finance careers. The curriculum allows for flexibility, enabling students to tailor their studies toward specific career paths in areas like banking, financial analysis, financial planning, and corporate finance. The program prepares graduates for roles such as financial analyst, loan officer, stockbroker, and portfolio manager.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance - Real Estate Concentration
Description: Real estate is a specialized area of finance designed for students who desire careers that specialize in residential, commercial or industrial real estate and related industries.  Since the real estate field is very broad, this concentration is designed to give students flexibility in selecting courses that fit their areas of interest.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Studies - Dietetics Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Health Studies with a Dietetics Concentration equips students with the knowledge and skills in communications, sciences, research, food, nutrition, management, and healthcare systems.  The program prepares students for various career paths, including graduate work in fields like clinical nutrition and dietetics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Studies - Exercise, Sport & Movement Sciences Concentration
Description: This program prepares students to use knowledge of functional anatomy and biomechanics to analyze and evaluate movement, prescribe exercises to prevent injuries, and enhance performance.  It also focuses on recognizing risk factors related to physical activity and nutrition, and understanding the principles of program planning and administration for health and wellness programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Studies - Health Sciences Concentration
Concentration: Health Sciences, Dietetics, Exercise, Sport and Movement Sciences, Healthcare Leadership
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Health Studies with a Health Sciences concentration provides the foundational knowledge and skills to develop, manage, and evaluate health initiatives.  It is grounded in health promotion theory and practice, offering flexibility through elective hours for students to tailor the program to their professional goals in various health fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Studies - Healthcare Leadership Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Health Studies with a Healthcare Leadership concentration provides comprehensive exposure to administration and leadership within the healthcare field.  The curriculum includes coursework in the healthcare environment, professionalism, leadership, business skills, and communication.  Upon graduation, students are prepared for advanced coursework in areas like healthcare administration and public health, or for employment in various settings such as hospitals, ambulatory care facilities, and government health agencies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in History at The University of Memphis introduces students to the richness and complexity of the human experience through a curriculum covering all major geographic areas and time periods.  The program aims to develop knowledge of the past and an appreciation for history as an intellectual discipline that uses various scholarly methodologies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Hospitality and Resort Management
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Hospitality and Resort Management program prepares students for leadership roles within the global hospitality industry, covering a wide range of topics including lodging, food service, tourism, and event planning.  The curriculum emphasizes a balance of academic knowledge and experiential learning to equip students with the necessary skills for success in the competitive hospitality business environment.  Mandatory field experiences and internships provide practical, real-world learning opportunities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Hospitality and Resort Management - Culinary Arts Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Hospitality and Resort Management with a Culinary Arts Concentration provides students with a comprehensive curriculum covering advanced culinary skills, pastry and baking, food analysis, and international cuisine.  The program is designed to equip students with the necessary knowledge and practical abilities for management roles within the food and beverage industry.  It combines theoretical learning with hands-on lab experience in areas like restaurant service and food production.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Hospitality and Resort Management - Lodging Management Concentration
Description: The primary goal of the Hospitality and Resort Management program is to produce graduates who have the knowledge and skills necessary for them to be successful in the increasingly competitive hospitality business environment. The program is committed to expanding the general business knowledge, specific hospitality skills, and overall technical competence of its students.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Education in Human Development and Learning
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Education in Human Development and Learning program's objectives are to promote child development and learning, build family and community relationships, and teach students to observe, document, and assess young children and families.  Successful completion of the program qualifies a person to apply for licensure in Early Childhood Education (PreK-3).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Human Resource Management
Concentration: Talent Management and Talent Acquisition, Learning and Development, Performance Management and Appraisal, Compensation and Total Reward Systems, Employee Well-being, Employment Law Compliance
Description: A BBA in Human Resource Management prepares students for a career in managing human resources in various sectors, including private or public organizations, government, and non-profits. As a human resource manager, graduates play a key role in staffing, training, development, and employee compensation. The program aims to make graduates immediately employable and prepared for a long-term career with advancement opportunities.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Federal, State, Institutional, Private

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International and Global Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in International and Global Studies provides an interdisciplinary education, integrating disciplines like Political Science, Economics, and History to foster a deep understanding of international societies and global systems. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in government, non-profits, and international organizations by focusing on global issues such as health, human rights, and economic development. Students are required to demonstrate competency in a modern foreign language and complete an internationally-related experiential learning activity.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in International Business
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) at the University of Memphis provides a foundational knowledge of business. While a specific major in International Business is not offered, students can pursue a Minor in International Business to gain skills for careers in the global marketplace.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism
Concentration: Broadcast Journalism, Creative Mass Media, Sports Media, Integrated Social Media
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Journalism at the University of Memphis trains students to become professionals in the news industry, working in various media outlets like magazines, newspapers, television stations, and online platforms.  The program emphasizes developing a core of writing and multimedia skills centered around effective and ethical storytelling.  Students have high flexibility to create a study plan that aligns with their career goals, and they are encouraged to pursue a minor.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, International grants and tuition waivers

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism - Broadcast Journalism
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Journalism with a concentration in Broadcast Journalism at the University of Memphis prepares students for professional roles in the broadcast news industry. Graduates often find employment at television stations, radio stations, and online news outlets in various capacities such as anchors, reporters, producers, and editors.  The program requires 51 credit hours within the Department of Journalism and Strategic Media.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism - Creative Mass Media Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Journalism with a Creative Mass Media concentration prepares students for careers as versatile creative media professionals. Graduates often work as art directors, audio/video editors, content producers, and social media managers. The curriculum combines coursework in journalism and strategic media with specialized training in graphic design or photography from the Department of Art and Design.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism - Sports Media Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Journalism with a Sports Media Concentration trains students for professional roles in the sports media industry. Graduates often find employment in athletic departments, team media offices, and news outlets as content creators, editors, photographers, producers, and social media managers. The curriculum combines coursework from Journalism and Strategic Media, Film & Video Production, and Sport & Leisure Management.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Liberal Studies in Liberal Studies, Asian Studies and International Trade
Description: The Bachelor of Liberal Studies (B.L.S.) with a focus on Asian Studies and International Trade is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to explore a wide variety of subjects. The curriculum is divided into General Education, Coordinated Study, Foreign Language (Chinese or Japanese), Area Studies focusing on East Asia, and International Economics and Business Studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Liberal Studies in Liberal Studies, Judaic Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Liberal Studies is an interdisciplinary program that allows for the study of multiple areas within the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. This degree provides flexibility and equips students with broad critical thinking and communication skills applicable to a variety of career fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Liberal Studies in Liberal Studies, Religious Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Liberal Studies (B.L.S.) in Religious Studies is designed for students with diverse backgrounds and interests. The program helps students develop skills in critical thinking, analysis of complex issues, and oral and written expression. It prepares graduates for various fields such as business, healthcare, social science, and the humanities, or for further study in a seminary or graduate program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Management
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) in Management is designed to develop the skills and knowledge needed to manage people and processes in organizations.  It emphasizes leading people and teams, strategic thinking and decision-making, planning and organizing, and human resource management.  The curriculum includes courses on communication, negotiation, critical thinking, and the ability to manage oneself and others.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Management, Entrepreneurship Concentration
Description: A management major with an entrepreneurship concentration emphasizes the development of knowledge and skills needed for owning and operating a business. This includes leading people and teams, planning and organizing, and creative and strategic thinking. The program prepares students for an entrepreneurial career through a combination of coursework and practical experience.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Management Information Systems
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) in Management Information Systems (MIS) prepares graduates for entry-level information systems positions with a foundation for career growth. The curriculum covers programming languages, computer hardware and system software, business systems analysis and development, data management, and networking. The program aims to equip students with the skills to manage an organization's information resources effectively.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Marketing
Concentration: Marketing Communications, Digital and Social Media Marketing, Marketing Analytics, Brand Management
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration in Marketing at the University of Memphis provides students with a deep understanding of consumer behavior and effective marketing strategies.  The curriculum covers core marketing facets such as communications, digital and social media strategy, analytics, sales, and brand management, alongside a broad foundation in general business principles.  This program is offered by the Fogelman College of Business & Economics, which is fully accredited by the AACSB.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences provides a foundation in calculus, linear algebra, and abstract mathematical structures. Students learn to use these techniques to solve problems, understand vector analysis, and apply calculus concepts to higher dimensions. The program aims to develop skills in reading, presenting, and formulating mathematical proofs, and using computers to solve mathematical problems.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences - Actuarial Science Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences with a concentration in Actuarial Science provides students with enhanced preparation for entry into the actuarial field. This degree is designed for those interested in the mathematics involved in risk management. Students in this program take courses in interest theory, mathematical statistics, and economics to prepare for the first two actuarial exams.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences - Data Science Concentration
Description: The Data Science concentration in Mathematical Sciences is designed to meet the high demand for data scientists by providing a strong foundation in both statistics and computer science. This program prepares students for careers in the field and for advanced studies in data science or applied statistics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences - Second Major
Concentration: Actuarial Sciences, Applied Mathematics, General Mathematics, Graduate Study in Mathematics, Secondary Mathematics Education, Applied Statistics, Data Science
Description: The Second Major in Mathematical Sciences is designed primarily for students whose first major is in a mathematically intensive field like Chemistry, Computer Science, Physics, or Engineering. It allows students to complement their primary field of study by completing 30 credit hours of specified mathematics courses. This program provides a strong quantitative background, enhancing career and graduate study opportunities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Alcohol and Drug Abuse Services
Description: The Bachelor of Professional Studies in Alcohol and Drug Abuse Services prepares students for careers providing services to those affected by alcohol and drug abuse, including individuals, families, and communities. The program welcomes prior work experience, which can be evaluated through portfolio assessment, and includes internships. Graduates often find careers in hospitals, social service agencies, and employee assistance programs, with some pursuing graduate-level education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Aviation Management
Description: The Bachelor of Professional Studies (B.P.S.) with a concentration in Aviation Management prepares students for careers as professional managers in the aviation industry.  The curriculum provides an understanding of organizations, administrative leadership, communication, conflict resolution, and operations management.  Graduates are prepared for roles in airlines, business flight operations, maintenance facilities, and with manufacturers and suppliers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Child Development and Family Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Professional Studies with a concentration in Child Development and Family Studies focuses on recognizing and enhancing important developmental milestones for children from birth through adolescence.  Students learn to create effective learning environments, assist parents in fostering positive relationships, and understand the influence of family, culture, peers, and schools on child growth.  The program, which does not lead to teacher licensure, also explores the importance of advocacy for children and their families in various settings like classrooms, hospitals, or the justice system.
ProgramCategory: Child Development##Family and Consumer Sciences##Human Development

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Child Life Specialist
Description: The Bachelor of Professional Studies in Child Life Specialist program prepares students for careers as child life specialists, who support children and families in coping with the challenges of hospitalization, illness, and disability.  The curriculum focuses on child development, therapeutic play, family engagement, and child advocacy to meet the emotional and psychological needs of children in healthcare settings.  A 600-hour unpaid clinical internship under the supervision of a Certified Child Life Specialist is required.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Construction Leadership
Description: The Bachelor of Professional Studies with a concentration in Construction Leadership aims to provide students with the essential skills and knowledge to become effective construction managers. The program is also designed to enhance the careers of practicing professionals in the construction industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Disability Studies and Rehabilitation Services
Description: The Bachelor of Professional Studies (B.P.S.) with a concentration in Disability Studies and Rehabilitation Services is designed for students seeking to be academically and professionally grounded in issues faced by individuals seeking disability services.  The program emphasizes employment, independent living outcomes, communication, and problem-solving within disability services.  A supervised field experience component allows students to integrate classroom principles and develop entry-level skills in a work setting.
ProgramCategory: Rehabilitation Science##Social Work and Human Services##Human Services##Rehabilitation Counseling

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Early Care and Learning Administration
Description: This program is designed for individuals seeking careers in the administration of early childhood programs, including childcare centers, pre-kindergarten programs, and Head Start.  The curriculum focuses on developing skills in fiscal management, personnel, health and safety, and public relations within early childhood settings.  This program does not lead to teacher licensure.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Early Intervention Specialist
Description: The Bachelor of Professional Studies with a concentration in Early Intervention prepares individuals to work with children ages 0-2 who have an identified developmental delay or disorder. Students learn to promote caregiver-child interaction by helping families adapt routines to support children's learning. The program introduces adult learning approaches and the impact of cultural diversity on family practices.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Health Services
Description: The Bachelor of Professional Studies (B.P.S.) in Health Services is designed for individuals looking to start or move up in the health services field.  This program suits both new students and experienced professionals from allied health backgrounds.  It provides a strong base in health services administration, focusing on healthcare management, patient care, communication, policy, risk management, and financial oversight.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Professional Studies in Professional Studies, Human Services
Description: The Bachelor of Professional Studies in Human Services is designed for students interested in the helping professions. The curriculum aims to develop a philosophical orientation to the human condition, enlarge understanding of social structures, and study human growth and development. Students take courses from departments like Counseling, Sociology, Social Work, Psychology, and Management.
ProgramCategory: Human Services##Social Work and Human Services##Interdisciplinary Studies

ProgramName: Minor in Accounting
Description: The Accounting Minor provides foundational and intermediate knowledge in accounting principles. There are two tracks: one for students within the Fogelman College of Business and Economics (FCBE) and another for students with majors in other colleges at the university.  The curriculum covers financial and managerial accounting, intermediate accounting, and individual tax compliance.

ProgramName: Minor in Advertising
Description: The minor in advertising at The University of Memphis introduces students to the skills and tools of the advertising field.  Its core curriculum provides a broad overview of advertising, while elective courses allow for specialization in a specific area of interest within the industry.

ProgramName: Minor in Aerospace Studies
Description: The Aerospace Studies Minor is designed for students interested in the academic aspects of the Air Force ROTC program without the obligation of pursuing a commission as an officer.  To be awarded the minor, a cadet must successfully complete 16 semester hours in Aerospace Studies with a minimum grade of 'C'.

ProgramName: Minor in African and African American Studies
Description: The African and African-American Studies program at the University of Memphis offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of African people in Africa and the Diaspora. Its mission is to help students develop a solid knowledge base in the field, along with analytical skills to understand historical and contemporary issues related to the experiences of Africans and African Americans.

ProgramName: Minor in Alcohol and Drug Abuse Services
Description: This interdisciplinary minor examines societal alcohol and drug abuse from the perspectives of anthropology, counseling, criminal justice, psychology, and sociology. The minor is open to students majoring in any area within any undergraduate college at The University of Memphis.
ProgramCategory: Social Sciences##Social Work and Human Services##Psychology##Sociology##Criminal Justice

ProgramName: Minor in American Sign Language
Description: The Minor in American Sign Language (ASL) is offered by the School of Communication Sciences and Disorders for students in various disciplines who are interested in learning and using ASL. This 18-credit hour program is intended to teach students the fundamentals of ASL and enrich their knowledge of Deaf Culture. Earning this minor does not prepare a student to work as a professional ASL interpreter.

ProgramName: Minor in American Studies
Description: The American Studies minor at the University of Memphis engages students in an examination of the culture and society of the United States, with attention paid to the ways in which Americans express their basic values and give meaning to their institutions and everyday social practices. This minor provides an opportunity to explore the commonalities and differences among Americans through an interdisciplinary course of study.

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology
Description: This minor provides a grounding in modern anthropology, including the basics of archaeology, biological anthropology, cultural anthropology, and linguistics. The focus of this minor is on providing a broad base for understanding anthropological theories and perspectives and is useful for any student interested in culture, culture change, or the ways that humans interact in and with the world.

ProgramName: Minor in Applied Behavior Analysis
Description: This 18-hour, 100% online minor provides foundational knowledge in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and prepares students for the national exam to become a certified Registered Behavior Technician (RBT). The program is designed to benefit students with career or educational goals in fields like Psychology, Counseling, and Social Work. It is particularly well-suited for majors in Teaching All Learners, Psychology, Social Work, and Child Development.

ProgramName: Minor in Art History
Description: The Minor in Art History at the University of Memphis requires the completion of 18 semester hours. This includes two foundational courses in world art and visual studies, supplemented by 12 semester hours of advanced 4000-level Art History courses.

ProgramName: Minor in Asian Studies
Description: The Asian Studies minor at the University of Memphis is designed for students interested in China and Japan, two of the United States's most significant global partners. The program aims to equip students with the necessary skills, including language and cultural fluency, to succeed in a global market with an Asian-related context. This minor combines language skills with historical and philosophical context to prepare students for success.

ProgramName: Minor in Banking and Financial Services
Description: The Banking and Financial Services Minor provides students with basic problem-solving and analytical tools necessary for success in various financial institutions, including banks, credit unions, securities firms, and investment banks. This rigorous field of study prepares students for career options such as Commercial Lending VP, Bank Manager, Investment Banker, and Portfolio Manager.

ProgramName: Minor in Biology
Description: The Biology Minor at the University of Memphis provides students with a foundation in biological concepts, requiring courses in General Biology I and II with their corresponding labs, followed by 10 upper-division hours. Students must achieve a grade of 'C-' or better in all biology courses applied to the minor.

ProgramName: Minor in Business Economics
Description: The Business Economics minor is for students with a major outside the Fogelman College of Business & Economics. It requires 18 semester hours in economics courses, including introductory macroeconomics and microeconomics, and 12 additional upper-division hours approved by the department chair.

ProgramName: Minor in Business Finance
Description: The Business Finance Minor is for students who wish to supplement their major with a foundational understanding of finance. The curriculum covers essential topics such as financial accounting, microeconomics, financial management, investments, and financial markets. The requirements differ based on whether the student's major is within the Fogelman College of Business and Economics or another college at the university.

ProgramName: Minor in Chemistry
Description: The Minor in Chemistry at the University of Memphis requires the completion of 20 semester hours in chemistry courses. This includes General Chemistry I and II with their corresponding labs, plus twelve additional semester hours in chemistry courses applicable to the major, which must include two laboratory courses.

ProgramName: Minor in Child Development
Description: The Child Development minor provides a foundational understanding of the biological, physical, socio-emotional, and cognitive growth of children from conception through adolescence. It is designed to complement many majors for students interested in careers involving children and families in various settings. The program aims to prepare students to work as agents of social change with diverse populations.

ProgramName: Minor in Classical Studies
Description: The undergraduate Minor in Classical Studies at the University of Memphis requires 18 credit hours, consisting of 9 hours of core courses and 9 hours of elective courses. The program is designed for students who wish to become familiar with Classical cultures and broaden their knowledge of the foundations of Western civilization. Students can choose from a wide range of courses in art history, classics, history, philosophy, and political science.

Description: UofM Global offers a wide selection of fully online undergraduate and graduate degree programs, providing students with flexible access to higher education across many high-demand sectors.  These programs are designed to be completed entirely online, allowing for the transfer of credits from other institutions.
